newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND BANK GOV WANTS SMALL 1998 PAY RISES - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND BANK GOV WANTS SMALL 1998 PAY RISES - PAPER.

text.p: Bank of Finland governor Sirkka Hamalainen was quoted as saying in an interview with Central Banking magazine received on Friday that Finnish pay rises in 1998 should be very small.

"Finland must not let wages rise too fast in good times and undermine our competitiveness again. It will be essential in the 1997 wage agreement to keep wage rises to very low levels," Hamalainen said.
Incomes settlement talks for the next pay deals due to take effect in February 1998 are scheduled to be held this autumn.

When asked whether Finland had taken a risk by linking the markka to Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) and might face prolonged recession because the exchange rate would no longer act as a safety valve, Hamalainen said:
"We can manage this as long as we have learnt the lessons of the past."
Although still dependent on the forest industry, the Finnish export sector was now less vulnerable to cyclical fluctuations than it used to be.
"With a few exceptions, the great majority of firms are strongly in favour of stable exchange rates," she said.

"There has been a tendency in Finland to resort to devaluations (within a basically fixed-rate regime) and this is bad for our economy. Companies now are in favour of exchange rate discipline, as they recognise that flexibility in our case usually means depreciation," Hamalainen said.

In such a scenario interest rates rise and this reduces incentives to invest. Finland's efforts to qualify for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) had yielded positive returns in the form of lower interest rates, she noted.
"We feel that the single currency will be very beneficial for a small country like Finland," she said.
"We expect this will provide a needed additional discipline for the economy and spur structural change," she added.
Hamalainen repeated her call for wage discipline.
"We must not let nominal wages rise too fast," she said.
"It is also crucially important for companies to strengthen their balance sheets and overall financial position," she added.
